cards.title: Planning, part II
pages:
Chapter 4 planned scope, time and cost. Chapter 5 plans the other knowledge areas: **quality, human resources, communications, risk and procurement**. Skipping them is a classic mistake: they matter as much to the project's success.
Our part: **quality** (quality management plan, quality metrics, quality checklists) and **human resources** (the human resource management plan).

debrief.A: You called it operations. This centre's first session is temporary and unique: a project inside the national program.
debrief.B: Project: temporary, with a unique result. The national Bac is the program around it.
debrief.C: Budget has nothing to do with it: temporary and unique makes a project.

cards.title: What is quality?
pages:
**ISO:** quality is "the degree to which a set of inherent characteristics fulfil requirements".
**Conformance to requirements:** the project's processes and products meet the written specifications.
**Fitness for use:** the product can be used as it was intended.
**The customer ultimately decides** whether the quality is acceptable.

debrief.A: It did conform. What failed was fitness for use.
debrief.B: Fitness for use: it met the rules but didn't work for the candidate. The customer decides.
debrief.C: It conformed, but a candidate couldn't use it: fitness for use failed.

cards.title: The quality management plan
pages:
**Quality planning:** identify which quality standards are relevant to the project and how to satisfy them, designing quality into the products and into the processes that manage the project.
A **quality management plan** typically covers: the **quality standards** that apply, the **metrics** used to measure them, **problem reporting and corrective action**, and **supplier quality**. Its size varies with the project.

debrief.A: Problem reporting and corrective action, and supplier quality, completed the plan.
debrief.B: Pens aside: the plan lacked problem reporting and supplier quality.
debrief.C: Nothing missing? Problem reporting and supplier quality were.

cards.title: Quality metrics and the project dashboard
pages:
A **metric** is a standard of measurement. Metrics let an organisation measure performance and compare it over time or with others.
A **project dashboard** is a graphical screen summarising the key project metrics.
**Best practice:** the best-performing organisations use a project management toolbox, grow competent project leaders, streamline delivery processes, and install a sound set of project performance metrics.

debrief.A: You measured people. The exam itself went unmeasured.
debrief.B: You measured the exam itself: on time, incidents, fraud detected.
debrief.C: The pass rate isn't yours to control, and it came after the project ended.

cards.title: Quality checklists
pages:
A **checklist** is a list of items to be noted or consulted. It helps the team verify that a set of required steps has been covered.
One project can have many: for interviewing team members, selecting suppliers, reviewing documents, **making sure a room is ready**.

debrief.A: The device line closed the gap at the gate.
debrief.B: Weather isn't a checklist item; devices were.
debrief.C: 'The supervisors will notice' is exactly what a checklist replaces.

cards.debrief_inspection: You made {right} of {total} calls right against the checklist. It catches what memory misses.

cards.title: Project HR management and the organisational chart
pages:
**Project human resource management** is about making effective use of the people involved in the project.
Its main planning output is the **human resource management plan**: a **project organisational chart**, a **responsibility assignment matrix**, a **resource histogram** and a **staffing management plan**.
A **project organisational chart** shows how authority and responsibility are distributed within the project. Its complexity follows the project's size.

debrief.A: Straight to the region skips the chart, and nobody nearby acts.
debrief.B: Deputy first: the chart shows who has authority.
debrief.C: Nearest isn't a reporting line. The chart is.

cards.title: The responsibility assignment matrix and RACI
pages:
A **responsibility assignment matrix (RAM)** maps the work in the **WBS** to the people responsible for it.
A **RACI chart** shows four roles per task: **Responsible** (does the task), **Accountable** (signs off, has the authority), **Consulted** (has the information needed), **Informed** (is told of the status or result).

debrief.A: One Accountable person: the envelopes were signed on time.
debrief.B: Two Accountables meant nobody signed. Exactly one A per task.
debrief.C: No Accountable person: the envelope sat unsigned.

cards.title: The resource histogram
pages:
A **resource histogram** is a column chart showing the number of resources needed for, or assigned to, a project over time.
Stacking the columns by skill shows the total needed each period; after assignment, it shows how each person's time is allocated.

debrief.A: You levelled the peak by borrowing staff, at a cost in budget.
debrief.B: You levelled the peak by crowding rooms, at a cost in fairness.
debrief.C: You cut the peak by thinning supervision, at a cost in integrity.

cards.title: The staffing management plan
pages:
A **staffing management plan** describes **when and how people are added to and removed from** the project.
It covers the types and numbers of people needed over time, and how they are **acquired, trained, rewarded and reassigned** after the project.

debrief.C: Equipment instead of people: it didn't catch the earpiece.
